newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Greece to start receiving Russian natgas next week.
newsitem.headline: Greece to start receiving Russian natgas next week.

text.p: Greece, which has completed the construction of its main gas pipeline, will next week receive its first deliveries of Russian natural gas via Bulgaria, a senior Greek official said on Monday.
The general manager of Greece's Public Gas Corp SA (DEPA), Spiros Paleoyannis, said that DEPA will start filling its main pipeline with Russian gas from September 16.

"Yesterday we signed in Greece a protocol on the procedure with Russia's Gasexport, Bulgaria's Bulgargas and (the Bulgarian-Russian) Topenergy joint stock company for the first quantity of gas from September 16," Paleoyannis told Reuters.
"We have completed the construction of the main pipeline and its infrastructure in Greece in order to supply DEPA's first customers," he said.
He did not say when DEPA would start distributing gas to its consumers.
Paleoyannis, who is attending a Balkan gas conference in Sofia, said that only some 600 million cubic metres of Russian gas would be supplied to Greece in 1997.
"We will start with symbolic quantities but they will increase to achieve 2.4 billion cubic metres per year by 2002," he said.
Greece's Prometheus Gas company is also expected to import additional quantities of Russian gas, Paleoyannis said.
Bulgaria completed its pipeline to the Greek border a year and a half ago and has been waiting for its neighbour to finalise the pipeline construction on its territory.
In addition to Greece, Bulgaria's transit gas network totalling some 2,000 km has links with Turkey and Macedonia. A new link with Serbia is also being constructed.
